text:
amy_sales: Heads up — POC with Acme Corp: when we send the aggregated doc set (~1.1MB, ~120k tokens) appended to the system prompt the API returns 413/Request Entity Too Large. They expected to ingest full conversation history. Blocking signature review. Anyone seen this?

olivia_support: Can you paste the exact error and request size? 1.1MB likely exceeds our request body limit for hosted tier.

amy_sales: Error from client: '413 Request Entity Too Large' with connection closed. No stack trace. Using /v1/generate with model 'redwood-13b-open' and max_tokens 1024. We gzip payload before sending.

raj_eng: 413 from edge — likely nginx or cloudfront limit. If you're gzipping the body, check Content-Length vs Transfer-Encoding. Also our API expects unchunked bodies; try streaming or multipart? Can you share curl?

amy_sales: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n -d @payload.json
```
payload.json ~1.1MB gzipped base64 in field 'context'

marta_solutions: For POCs we usually recommend chunking context into 50–100k token windows and use retrieval to fetch relevant chunks. Also we support prefix KV caching on Dedicated — but hosted has request body limits.

raj_eng: Two quick tests: 1) send a minimal payload with a short prompt to confirm API returning expected response 2) send the large payload but without gzip/base64 (raw json) to see where it's rejected. Also check response headers for 'x-edge-error' or 'x-nginx-proxy'

olivia_support: If this is enterprise customer wanting whole history inline we can suggest: a) use embeddings + rerank to compress context b) switch to Dedicated where we can raise the body limit/multipart streaming c) use our 'context-upload' presigned endpoint (beta) to upload large contexts and pass a context_id.

amy_sales: Customer is pushing back — legal wants full chat transcript with system prompt included. Can we enable context-upload for POC? Who owns that?

raj_eng: I can enable context-upload for the sandbox account. Need account id and thread. It will surface a presigned URL; then you call:
POST /v1/context/upload { "url": "...", "context_id": "acme-2026-03" }
and in generate call pass context_id instead of inline 'context'.

amy_sales: Perfect. Account id 98765. Can you toggle and send instructions? cc @marta_solutions for handoff.

infra-bot: config-change: context-upload enabled for account 98765 by raj_eng at 2026-03-20T15:04:12Z

marta_solutions: I'll run the playbook and send sample payload. Also suggest interim workaround: truncate older messages and include a 2-sentence summary of history to keep legal happy while we finish upload.

olivia_support: :thumbsup: Let me know if they still hit errors after using context_id. If so we'll escalate to infra.
